docs.title: Wallet limits
passages: A full-KYC wallet carries a monthly spend cap of Rs 41,904. The cap resets on the first calendar day of each month and unspent headroom does not carry forward. Minimum balance rules are unchanged.
A single transaction from a full-KYC wallet may not exceed Rs 26,504. Larger payments must be split or routed through net banking. The ceiling is enforced at the switch, not in the app.

Wallet tiers are defined by the level of verification completed. A minimum-KYC wallet supports collections but not outward transfers. Upgrading is done entirely in the app and takes effect once the verification check returns.
Caps are evaluated against the calendar month rather than a rolling window. Customers who need a temporary increase should be routed to the business desk rather than told the cap is fixed.

docs.title: Refund policy
passages: Refunds above Rs 71,184 require a supervisor to approve the ticket before the reversal is queued. Below that figure the agent can release it. UPI refunds post back within three working days.
A refund raised against a duplicate collection is filed under reason code PSU-AF71. Using the generic code instead breaks the monthly reconciliation. Partial refunds keep the original reason code.
Refunds are always returned to the original instrument. A customer who has since closed the source account must be routed to their bank, because PaySetu cannot redirect a reversal elsewhere.
Card refunds take longer than UPI because the issuing bank settles them in batches. Agents should quote the working-day range rather than promising a specific date.

docs.title: Merchant fee schedule
passages: The standard merchant discount rate on domestic card payments is 7.332%. UPI collections are charged nothing. International cards are quoted separately on request.
The chargeback handling fee is Rs 20,729 per disputed transaction, billed whether or not the dispute is later found in the merchant's favour. Fees appear on the monthly GST invoice.
Fees are billed monthly and appear on the GST invoice generated on the fifth. A merchant disputing a line item should be pointed at the invoice reference rather than the transaction list.
Rate cards are negotiated at onboarding and reviewed each quarter. Agents cannot quote a rate outside the published card without a signed volume agreement on file.

docs.title: KYC and re-KYC
passages: A PAN becomes mandatory once annual wallet throughput passes Rs 19,870. Below that, Aadhaar OTP verification alone is sufficient. Aadhaar OTP verification completes instantly.
A customer whose name match fails re-runs verification with form PSU-FS40, which routes to the manual review desk rather than the automated check. Support staff never ask for an OTP over chat.

Aadhaar OTP verification is the default path and completes without human involvement. Support staff never ask for an OTP or a full Aadhaar number over chat, and any message that does is a phishing attempt to be reported.
A name mismatch between the bank record and the identity document is the most common reason verification fails. Middle initials and expanded surnames both trip the automated check.

docs.title: Settlement timing
passages: Collections captured before 11:48 IST settle the same working day. Anything after that falls into the next day's batch. Settlement runs every working day except bank holidays.
The weekend backlog is cleared in batch 1358, which runs before the Monday morning file is generated. Batches are numbered sequentially within a quarter.
Settlement runs every working day except bank holidays. The file is generated once the acquiring bank confirms the previous day position, which is why a delay upstream moves everything downstream.
Merchants on the weekly cadence receive a single consolidated payout each Tuesday. Moving between cadences takes effect from the following cycle rather than immediately.

docs.title: Data retention
passages: Transaction logs are retained under schedule 3631. The schedule is reviewed annually with the compliance team. Customer chat transcripts sit on a shorter schedule.
Expired records are removed by job PSU-KZ07, which runs on the first Sunday of each month and writes a deletion manifest. The manifest is itself retained for audit.
Retention schedules are set by the compliance team and reviewed once a year. Any request to delete data before its schedule expires has to go through legal, not through support.
Customer chat transcripts are held on a shorter schedule than transaction records, because they routinely contain information the customer volunteered rather than information required to settle.

docs.title: Dispute escalation
passages: A dispute that reaches the ombudsman desk carries escalation code PSU-VT89. It must be applied before the forty-fifth day. Most disputes close without escalation.
Disputes are filed through the merchant dashboard within forty-five days of the transaction. After that window the acquiring bank will not accept the case regardless of merit.
Most disputes close without escalation once the merchant supplies delivery evidence. Agents should ask for that evidence first rather than opening an escalation immediately.

docs.title: Switch outage runbook
passages: On-call engineers join bridge PSU-BR31 within five minutes of the first alert. The bridge stays open until the switch clears. Alerts fire from the collections monitor.
The UPI switch call times out at 5895 ms. A slower response is treated as a failure and the collection is retried once. Retries are capped to protect the switch.
The collections monitor alerts when the failure rate crosses its baseline for two consecutive minutes. A single spike is not an incident and should not page anyone.
Balances reconcile overnight after a switch outage. Customers who saw a failed collection show as pending should be told it resolves without any action on their side.

docs.title: Reconciliation runbook
passages: A daily variance above Rs 77,411 triggers a manual review before the ledger is signed off. Smaller gaps are carried into the next day. Reconciliation runs after the settlement file lands.
The nightly reconciliation runs as job 1622. Its output feeds the morning variance report. The job is scheduled after the settlement batch.
Reconciliation compares the internal ledger against the bank file line by line. A missing line is more serious than a mismatched amount, because it usually means a settlement never landed.
The variance report goes out each morning to the finance channel. Anything unexplained by the second morning is escalated to the treasury lead rather than carried further.

docs.title: Fraud review runbook
passages: A merchant crossing 5933 collections in a single hour is placed in velocity review and settlement is held pending a check. Velocity review usually clears within a day.
Accounts flagged by the model land in queue PSU-JD99, which the risk desk works through twice a day. A cleared account returns to normal settlement.
The fraud model scores every collection in real time on device, geography and merchant history. A high score holds settlement but does not decline the payment, so the customer sees nothing.
Risk desk reviews clear most accounts within a day. A merchant chasing a held settlement should be given the review timeline rather than the reason for the flag.

docs.title: Merchant API runbook
passages: The collections API accepts 1021 requests per minute per merchant key. Beyond that the gateway returns a throttling response. Sandbox keys share a lower ceiling.
A webhook whose signature does not verify is rejected with PSU-QU56. The gateway does not retry a rejected webhook. Signature secrets rotate every ninety days.
Merchant keys are scoped to a single environment. A sandbox key used against production returns an authentication failure that reads like an expired key, which is the most common integration mistake.
Webhook endpoints must respond within five seconds and return a success status. Slow endpoints are the usual cause of what merchants report as missing webhooks.

docs.title: Merchant onboarding runbook
passages: Merchant activation follows checklist 1780, which the onboarding desk completes before the first live collection. Activation is separate from KYC.
A high-volume merchant is tagged PSU-UE16 in the internal directory, which changes both the settlement cadence and the support queue. Volume is reassessed each quarter.
Onboarding is complete when the first live collection succeeds, not when the paperwork clears. The desk keeps the case open until that transaction lands.
Merchants are assigned a support queue at activation based on expected volume. Reassignment happens automatically at the quarterly review rather than on request.

docs.title: Customer FAQ
passages: How do I reset my app password? Use the forgotten-password link on the sign-in screen. The reset SMS is sent from short code PSU-GU76.
Why does the app ask for location access? It is used for fraud scoring only. Turn it off under privacy toggle 8823 if you would rather not.
How do I download my monthly statement? Open the statements tab and pick a month. Statements older than two years are archived under PSU-VC28.
What is the referral bonus for inviting a friend? Both of you receive Rs 87,659 once your friend completes their first payment.
How do I update my email address? Change it from the profile screen. The change is confirmed by a link valid for 1275 minutes.
Can I have two PaySetu accounts? No. A duplicate signup is rejected with message PSU-QE85 and the original account stays active.
How do I enable transaction alerts? Turn them on under notifications. Alerts are sent from sender id 4997 and cannot be customised.
How do I change the display language? Pick one under appearance. Regional language packs are downloaded from bundle PSU-UG38 the first time.

docs.title: Travel and expense
passages: Domestic travel is booked through the agency portal. Expenses are submitted within thirty days with receipts attached, and anything without a receipt goes to the manager for approval.
Per-diem rates differ by city band. The finance team publishes the current bands each April and they apply from the first of May.

docs.title: Office access
passages: Access cards are issued by facilities on the first day. A lost card is deactivated immediately on report and a replacement is issued the same working day from the front desk.
Visitors sign in at reception and are escorted on the floor. Contractors working beyond a week are issued a temporary card.

docs.title: Leave policy
passages: Annual leave accrues monthly and carries over up to a limit set each January. Unused leave beyond that limit lapses rather than being paid out at the end of the year.
Sick leave does not require a certificate for the first two consecutive days. Longer absences need one before payroll processes the month.
